criteria.local_only_remodel: Refuse every imported containment target as today and convert all 20 declarations into explicit reference fields with manually stated team equality, policies and uniqueness. Cross-package lifecycle questions disappear because cross-package containment does. The audit cost is the steepest of the four: each parent.parent chain and each row.parent.* policy rewritten per site with fresh parity witnesses, and the drafts' explicit choice of canonical parents over copied identity is discarded at maximum migration expense without a proven unsafety behind the refusal.
criteria.owner_consent_facet: Admit imported containment only beneath parents whose owning package publishes an explicit containment endorsement, granting complete local semantics under endorsed parents and keeping a rejection that points at the missing endorsement otherwise; bound remote parents stay rejected unconditionally. The endorsement could bound depth, pick cascade or orphan behavior, and list exposed reverse collections, but none of that expressiveness is settled. Cost: a new declaration kind plus visibility and compatibility rules, mandatory edits in three owner packages with consumers queued behind their releases, and a gate that guards no real boundary here since all parents are same-project packages, while offering nothing for genuinely remote atomicity.
criteria.plain_import_containment: Treat a plain import as the same deployment: the child keeps its own package identity, inherits team and storage from the imported parent, and receives the full local lifecycle (immutable parent binding, atomic subtree archive and delete, parent-scoped uniqueness, queryable reverse collections, index-wide cycle errors). Bound parents remain forbidden. The gamble is coupling: a consumer's archive can sweep owner-adjacent children, a future package split quietly breaks the atomicity story, foreign readability must be fenced, and the engine has not yet demonstrated the promised same-store atomic subtree commit nor any diagnostic for the split day.
criteria.reference_scoping: Keep the parent link, the team and storage inheritance and the parent-scoped uniqueness, but cut the lifecycle cord: archiving or deleting a parent never touches imported children, and reverse collections become derived lookups instead of stored edges. Per-package archiving stays simple and no cross-store promise is ever uttered. The hazard is semantic divergence hiding behind identical syntax: deletion behaves one way for local children and another for imported ones, authors will presume cascade and be wrong, the orphan question (block the archive or strand readable children) has no draft answer, and cascade anywhere becomes bespoke per-app construction.

containment_rule.instructions: Which containment rule carries the least total risk across coupling fragility, silent behavior splits, migration volume and proof burden, while holding every accepted workflow and every negative intact? Weigh each option against the same workflow set and the same unknowns.

request.state: Twenty CanLang declarations in the draft corpus nest a child inside a parent owned by another package: Employee parents Expense, Leave and Onboard structures; Customer parents Invoice and Propose structures; Location parents Reception policy; further Service and minor sites follow the same shape. Provenance is uniform: all 20 parents enter by plain import, and not one bound from= import in the corpus (76 lines surveyed) serves as a containment parent, leaving remote containment a purely hypothetical axis. The six affected workflows are accepted as intended, including three-level nests whose defaults and policies climb parent.parent chains and read row.parent.* fields. Evidence on lifecycle intent is a clean zero: all 20 sites were read for delete/archive expectations and none states any, with four near-misses that decide nothing. The storage contract describes one atomic owner commit on one store covering included imports, yet subtree-spanning deletion is unimplemented, generated writes still travel an interim commit route, and deployment-split failures have a specified fail-before-commit behavior with no emitted diagnostic. Owner endorsement machinery does not exist and owner willingness cannot be read from sources. Cycles must keep failing, imports must grant no mutation rights over parents, and no option may be picked by discounting its documented worst case: split-atomicity exposure, two-faced deletion, remodel-everything cost, or release-coupled consent without atomicity value. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation result.
